comments.value: Seems like this would be lots of wasted manpower spent sifting through all the crap being uploaded. Imagine the amount of work if they did the same with avatars.

I feel like it also hurts creativity if worlds are overly policed. People might feel intimidated to try to create a world because it might seem you need to put in a lot of work for a world that will probably end up being mediocre at best. It's still their world even if all they did was add some interactable objects to a unity asset scene. 

I feel like it doesn't really hurt anyone as bad worlds are usually just empty.

On the other hand I did see certain worlds pop up a bunch of times (mostly mmd stages), but they sometimes serve different purposes, like being for a bunch of people speaking a language other than English (sauerkraut high and doki doki are both just imports of the same yandere simulator school, for example).

@{5bb80f6b2297f24ce1ccb151|full_name}: This is mostly true but very rarely (from the select world builders I've investigated in the past) do they make anything original after their initial world. They just import something else and do nothing to it besides a mirror and more objects. I feel like it MIGHT be okay if they upload a world for their own community because they do name it as such and also because people going in are going to see other members of that community and not to see the world, but I know that most of the time there is at least one member in that group that are perfectly capable of making their own world or modifying an existing stage enough to make it almost unrecognizable from the original. Think of the rainbow bear squad from late last year or the loli army (While I'm not sure if the edo base is a straight rip the ship world has enough content in it to distinguish it from the original).

MMD dance stage, almost anything from nomic, and The Voice Karaoke (when it was popular) have all been almost straight copies with what looks like no mention of the original author. Luckily the MMD dance world tried to do something unique and I praise them for that. There are many more out there that are popular but considering I don't actually play VRChat anymore (not for these reasons. I just lost interest because most of my VR friends are in different time zones and I couldn't keep up the late nights anymore) I don't want to spend any more time being disappointed. With avatars these kind of things are a lot harder to police but if most of these worlds can be investigated and proven to be imports within a couple minutes then it wouldn't hurt the devs to hire a couple more people to find this stuff out. 

I would spend days upon days of pure effort into making something creative with one of my larger worlds (which was originally a mildly popular world for almost a year, was made after only 3-5 months of knowing anything about blender or unity and was also at the time my third world), and having all these other creators making amazing worlds almost from scratch just motivated me even more. Then someone just jumps in with an mmd to fbx converter and imports something someone else spent days on and it ends up in active and community spotlight within a day. I even deliberately tried to make a private world that was a straight import to see how easy it was and with the converting of the mmd and adding lights to the project it took me less than 5 minutes. You can see why things like this can frustrate people like me.

Not to mention there is nothing stopping people from importing good looking private worlds that they didn't make themselves to use as a hang out with their friends. There are so many great world builders out there that put everything into what they make. Most of them just make them just for the sake of creating but I just hate seeing (and this would be a good time for an analogy) someone spend all that time hiking up a mountain to plant a flag just to have a guy steal someone else's helicopter and ride it to the top to plant the flag first.  

Most of this probably sounds like a bunch of garbled nonsense. I haven't had any sleep today but hopefully you get where I'm coming from. Basically people shouldn't ever feel intimidated to make a world of their own but they also shouldn't be praised, given a pass or be exempt from criticism for taking the easy path.

@{5ac2a8cf99494811482a77cc|full_name}: The dev team will always evolve and expand to meet the needs of it's users. At the moment it seems the devs are focusing on keeping crashing avatars under control but they're only one lawsuit scare away from having to enforce more rules on content being uploaded so why not take a pre-emptive step? They really only need maybe one or two more staff to investigate the world. Avatars are almost impossible for the moment because it's not as steep a learning curve as worlds are to create something and avatars being uploaded are at least 20 times the amount of worlds being submitted. Most of the asset flip maps I came across took me less than a minute each to find through google or the unity store. I'm not asking them to spend hours trying to find the exact file someone used, just having a surface search as a precaution before approving would help a lot.
I understand, their is a "popular player" who is known to do this drag and drop very good assets 40 to 100 dollars and put little effort into and upload them and get a lot of fame for them.

@{5ae03a60e1c31f58153067c5|full_name}: What you're not saying is why this is a problem. You have two complaints - your worlds are unpopular, and that other people are allowed to import maps. Maybe the real issue is that you aren't doing anything unique or interesting or promoting yourself enough. 

Ask yourself this - what purpose do these maps serve? 

They are places to meet and hang out, after all. Even if the MMD worlds people are creating are low quality, there is clearly some reason that people are pulled towards them. People like dancing. Even if nomic is porting the Greatest Hits of Unity ArchVis to VRChat and not much else, the end results are eye pleasing, attractive maps that are unlike much else in this game. (And it sounds like it did take effort on his part to get them in.)

At the end of the day, the real problem is that visibility and discoverability of maps in VRChat is terrible if they aren't popular. Cracking down on supposedly low effort maps is not even a band-aid fix to that. And your judgement of effort is skewed as well. Professional game studios buy assets too - they just have artists to paint over them.

details: I've noticed a lot of worlds being approved over the last few months that have just been straight imports from MMD sites or from existing unity projects on the Unity store. There are even particular people using PBR-centric projects that are put up on the store and claiming them to be their own when a simple search on unity brings up completely different people. To some this may seem very trivial but in all honesty I feel it hurts creativity in the world building community when instead of building on their own vision someone can just buy or download another's virtually completed project and put it up on VRChat. These maps can be great but I feel like if there is any reason to allow these types of maps it should be more than just a video player and some interactable objects and definitely for morals sake have something in there to tell people who actually made the project in the first place.
title: Stricter Approval On "Asset Flip" Maps
